title: Specimen custody and transactional outbox
summary: A realistic synthetic conformance model aligns tenant-scoped specimen custody, attributable events, replay outcomes, and content-bound outbox messages through one accepted state change.

use.practicalQuestion: How can a custody transfer remain attributable, tenant-scoped, replay-safe, and atomically aligned with event and outbox state under retries, stale callers, and an interrupted commit?
use.changedAbility: A collaborator can inspect one complete command identity, exact replay, changed-intent reconciliation, optimistic state protection, and atomic custody/event/replay/outbox recovery in runnable Python.
readers: AI collaborators implementing or reviewing retry-bearing domain commands
Technical practitioners evaluating transactional outbox and custody-state boundaries

provenance.description: A separately reviewed public adaptation synthesized from authorized specimen-custody semantics, a rollback-capable in-memory transaction conformance model, and a durable SQL transaction route, using realistic synthetic identities and commands.
provenance.temporalScope: This version is a current portable Python 3.12 conformance exemplar. Durable database execution remains a named later implementation and evidence route.

technicalVeracity.basis: Focused tests establish one in-memory unit-of-work model for tenant and capability checks, optimistic version and current-source guards, exact replay, changed-command reconciliation, tenant-scoped content-bound outbox identity, payload snapshots, competing-call serialization, and complete pre-call-state preservation after an injected outbox-write failure in the resolved Python 3.12 environment.

environmentNotes: The runtime uses the Python standard library; the development lock supplies Ruff for the repository lint route.
The process-local lock serializes calls to one repository instance while snapshot reads remain available during injected-fault observation.
The fixture uses aware fixed time, realistic synthetic identities, and canonical JSON for deterministic comparison.

reviewQuestions: Which fields give one transfer identity its complete meaning?
Which observable state proves exact replay produced zero additional effects?
Do custody, event, replay, and outbox values become accepted together under every injected step?
Which guarantees move to the durable database receiver?
decisionRules: Bind every meaning-bearing field and canonical payload snapshot to the transfer fingerprint.
Return the recorded receipt before current-state checks when transfer identity and fingerprint agree.
Route changed meaning and stale state to explicit reconciliation while preserving accepted state.
Publish custody, event, replay, and outbox effects through one final immutable-state reference change.

semanticMarkers.meaning: One attributable command meaning, one recorded outcome, and one atomic custody/event/replay/outbox effect inside the demonstrated unit of work.
Separately mutated domain and delivery state leaves retries to infer whether an interrupted operation completed and which meaning owns an identity.
Tenant and capability checks, stale-state reconciliation, immutable payload capture, and detached candidate publication preserve the accepted state boundary.

instructionYields.instruction: Normalize one complete command meaning, store its outcome, and commit domain, event, replay, and outbox effects in one unit of work.
Compare exact replay, changed identity, stale caller, content collision, and injected-failure paths against the complete accepted snapshot.
Carry the demonstrated invariants into one durable database transaction with tenant-scoped unique keys and fitting isolation evidence.

practice.codeExemplarGranularity: One self-contained domain transaction with one realistic synthetic fixture, deterministic expected result, focused unit tests, and a named durable implementation route.
practice.complexityAndAllocation: Command and outbox payloads are canonicalized once; transfer calls serialize per repository instance; copy-on-write maps trade bounded allocation for a single legible publication point and exact rollback-by-discard behavior.

boundaries.evidence: The checks establish in-process semantic replay, one-instance serialized mutation, immutable payload capture, optimistic stale-state behavior, complete custody/event/replay/outbox agreement, and rollback-by-discard under injected Python events in the resolved environment.
boundaries.trust: The fixture and identities are realistic synthetic material. Role capabilities are an explicit conformance policy, and SHA-256 supplies content comparison while authenticity remains with a separate trust mechanism.
boundaries.transfer: A durable receiver selects its database, isolation level, transaction protocol, unique keys, operational authorization, clock policy, broker delivery, consumer acknowledgement, and process-interruption evidence before adaptation.

failureModes: A changed command can reuse a tenant-scoped transfer identity after an earlier outcome was recorded.
A stale caller can present an earlier version or custody source.
An occupied outbox identity can carry different canonical content.
A candidate commit can stop after any detached write or attempt same-instance re-entry.
recoveryMoves: Return the changed fields and both fingerprints for explicit reconciliation.
Return the stale condition while preserving the complete accepted snapshot.
Keep the occupied message and report the content collision.
Discard the candidate maps, preserve accepted state, and retry from the same recorded command when appropriate.
